title: ASSIGNMENT – 3
subtitle: Breast Cancer Classification using Support Vector Machine
name: Srikrishna O S

sections.heading: AIM
sections.paragraph: To implement a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier for breast cancer diagnosis using a real-world breast cancer prediction dataset (breast_cancer_prediction.csv), evaluate classification performance with multiple kernels (linear, polynomial, RBF, sigmoid), tune hyperparameters using GridSearchCV with 5-fold stratified cross-validation, and compare the models using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC-AUC, confusion matrices, and ROC curves. The target variable is Biopsy_Result (Benign / Malignant), and the experiment also includes data inspection, missing-value imputation, standardization, and misclassification analysis. Libraries used: pandas, numpy, matplotlib, seaborn, scikit-learn.

sections.heading: DATASET DESCRIPTION
sections.paragraph: The Breast Cancer Prediction dataset consists of 10,000 patient records with clinical and diagnostic attributes (21 columns: demographics like Age, Gender and BMI, lifestyle factors like Smoking, Alcohol_Consumption and Physical_Activity, clinical measurements like Tumor_Size_cm, Blood_Pressure and Cholesterol, and an annual income field). The target variable is Biopsy_Result (Benign / Malignant), making this a binary classification problem. Patient_ID is a unique identifier column and carries no predictive information.

sections.heading: DATA PREPROCESSING
sections.subheading: Missing values, irrelevant features, encoding, and standardization
paragraph: Missing values: BMI, Tumor_Size_cm, Hormone_Therapy, Physical_Activity and Alcohol_Consumption each have 300 missing values (~3% each); all other columns have none. Missing numerical values are imputed with the median of each column computed only from the training set, then applied to both train and test, because the median is robust to outliers in skewed clinical measurements. Fitting the imputation on the training set only avoids data leakage from the test set.
Irrelevant features: Patient_ID is unique for every row (10000 unique values), so it is removed; all other columns are retained since none is constant or purely identifier-like.

Encoding and standardization: the categorical (object) columns are one-hot encoded with pd.get_dummies(drop_first=True) because they are nominal categories with no natural order. After encoding, the feature set has 22 columns. The data is split 80-20 (stratified on the target) into 8000 training and 2000 test samples, and StandardScaler is applied (fit on train, transform both) because SVM is a distance-based algorithm and unscaled features would dominate the margin computation.

sections.heading: OBSERVATIONS
bullets: Missing values are imputed with training-set medians only, avoiding data leakage.
Patient_ID is removed as an irrelevant identifier feature.
Categorical features are one-hot encoded before model training.
Features are standardized using StandardScaler before fitting the SVM.
All four kernels are compared under identical preprocessing.
Hyperparameters (C, gamma, degree) are tuned with GridSearchCV using 5-fold stratified CV.
RBF is the best kernel: test accuracy 0.9380, ROC-AUC 0.9756, F1 score 0.8364.
124 samples out of 2000 test rows are misclassified by the best (RBF) kernel.

sections.heading: CONCLUSION
sections.paragraph: An SVM classifier was implemented for breast cancer diagnosis using the Breast Cancer Prediction dataset. Data preprocessing - irrelevant feature removal, categorical one-hot encoding, training-based median imputation, and feature standardization - was applied before training. Four kernels (Linear, Polynomial, RBF, Sigmoid) were compared before and after hyperparameter tuning. Based on the test-set results, the RBF kernel with C=1 and gamma=scale performed best with a testing accuracy of 0.938 and an ROC-AUC of 0.976, making it the most suitable choice for this classification task.

I used GridSearchCV with StratifiedKFold to tune C, gamma, and degree.
I evaluated models using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and ROC-AUC, and identified RBF as the best kernel.
